kinds.d: A unique print pulled from ink or paint on a smooth, featureless plate; any second 'ghost' pull is weaker.

x.d: The earliest monotypes: brushed black-field images wiped to white, often night scenes.
Monotypes wiped, scraped and scratched by Degas, often reworked after printing.
x.dt: first vs cognate (ghost) pull · reworked or not

x.d: A line image made by drawing on the back of paper laid on an inked sheet, the drawing often surviving on the verso.

v.d: British Museum 1968,0210.31; pencil drawing on verso

x.dt: recto print · verso drawing · ink colour

kinds.d: A one-of-a-kind impression from a plate with fixed features (lines or textures) that recur, varied each time by inking or additions.
A print from a plate built by gluing materials such as card, fabric or string to a rigid board, inked as relief, intaglio or both.

x.d: Collagraphs from glued-up plates as developed and named by Glen Alps in the 1950s.

kinds.a: blind embossing · inkless intaglio · relief print
kinds.d: An image made by pressing damp paper into a carved or built-up plate so the design stands in relief, mainly without ink. Embossing added to an inked print is not this.

x.d: Thin lead sheet pressed into relief from the artist's models and mounted like a print, published as an edition.

x.a: Paper Pools · cast and pressed paper pulp
x.d: Images formed in coloured paper pulp poured and pressed in moulds, made with master printer Kenneth Tyler.

v.n: Paper Pools (e.g. A diver, paper pool 17)

x.dt: single sheet vs multi-panel · colour variant

brands.d: Genoese artist credited with inventing monotype in the 1640s.
French artist who made and reworked many monotypes.
French artist who developed the traced monotype.
American printmaker who named and developed the collagraph.

Kenneth Tyler's print workshop where Hockney made the Paper Pools in 1978.
